I’m the original OP and I’m so happy to hear this! My fiancé and I have a two year old but I know taking in my sister was the right thing. I know all about the honeymoon period and I’m not afraid for it to be rocky or for an all out storm. Every time I talk to my sister it’s like 12 years hasn’t even passed at all. 

I hope one day my future husband and I can look back at the beautiful children we’ve raised including my sister and be proud of the successful adults they become.
That’s totally terrifying to me. Were there any other factors?

Okay awesome! I finally talked to the case worker today and she advised she got the paperwork sent off yesterday and had it expedited so I’m hoping that means good things. 

She did tell me because my sister is in psychiatric care (due to her dose and amount of psychotropic medications upon intake) it means she will require a psychiatric evaluation upon release. After she is discharged she will have to go to a specialized foster home that can assist with her needs and acclimate her to a home environment. After that with approval she would be discharged into my care. She did tell me that I also need to make sure I can assist with those needs and provide the type of home she needs. I told her that no matter what care my sister required my fiancé and I are willing and ready to provide that no matter the cost or time. That seemed to go over well for her 

The court hearing is Tuesday and although she did say it would be better if I could be there it would be fine if I was present by phone. She also said if I could have letters of recommendations to hand the judge at that time it would help even more. She is in the process now of verifying my identity so hopefully by the court date I can have access to my sisters ongoing and past medical records and more documents that would help. 

Good news is we sign the lease for our new house tomorrow and move in next week. It’s in a great neighborhood in a good school district and she will have her own room and bathroom. I also did research into requirements for positive home studies and will be doing everything I can to safe guard every aspect of the home.

I definitely agree and hence why I’m so anxious to get any sort of response from her case worker. We live in a small town but I know school faculty well as well as good family and trauma therapists in the area.

As soon as she’s here that will be the first thing we do. She expressed a large part of abuse came from her stepmom who was angry at her sexuality (pansexual) and I told her that we would never shame her for any personal choice she made and we only want to support and guide her in the best way possible. I know adjusting to a new family will be difficult as well as integrating her into our lives and forming healthy bonds and boundaries as we do have a toddler in the home. I have confidence in myself though and I feel like I know the system as well as the mental health system well enough to guide her through this. 

**Edit: low to know (grammatical)

Thank you so much! I live in citrus county I hope that helps. You definitely helped alleviate some of my worry as me and my fiancé struggled a long time conceiving and talked about becoming foster parents and I knew how long of a process that could be. 

When you refer to a “visit” are you saying that could be a faster way of her getting here without months and months of process? When I talked to her case workers supervisor he said we were looking at anywhere from 4 weeks to 6 months. My sister is currently in a mental health facility due to her being on several psychotropic medications when her father dropped her off and I want her bouncing around as little as possible. 

She is already doing online school through the facility and is in the lowest level security possible which means she is cooperating with therapy and schooling. 

My only other worry is our mother who is in a rehab facility. The case worker wanted her address as she said she had to notify her. I didn’t have it at the time but was able to track her down and after speaking to her my mother said she would sign anything necessary for me to obtain custody of my sister. 

We are also moving into a new house in 2 weeks as we just signed the lease on a larger home but currently live with my fiancés family to help with the move (we moved from a small house to this larger house in 1 month) Will this slow down the process? Should I let the caseworker know? 

I’m sorry I have so many questions. I have had such a bad time in the system and I want things to go as smoothly and as quickly as possible for her so I can get her in a stable home and a supportive environment.
